note: GSV and SSV are the instructions this adapter has got wrong the most times, and every previous fix was verified against tools/l5x rather than against the adapter. Four separate facts are asserted here. (1) GSV writes its LAST operand, not a fixed index. (2) SSV writes a CIP system object, not a tag, so its last operand is a READ and it emits no write edge at all. (3) GSV operand 1 is the object instance name, a KEYWORD - rung 1 names it Conveyor_Drive, which is also a declared tag, exactly as in the corpus where every resolvable GSV instance name was a module and the tag matching it was that module's alias. Typing operand 1 as TAG emits a false read edge there, which is the failure ADR-013 section 7 rules out. (4) An omitted operand is a HOLE, not an absent slot: rung 0 writes GSV(WallClockTime,,DateTime,Dest) with an empty instance name, and dropping that slot renumbers every operand after it, silently retyping the rest of the instruction. Teeth: reverting any one of the four changes an edge here.
